paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. The Pharisees came with a question about what a man is ALLOWED to do. Jesus answered with what God made marriage to BE. They asked about the edge of the cookie sheet, and He pointed at the whole bakery (Mark 10:2, 10:6).

Jesus says Moses wrote that certificate of divorce "because of your hardness of heart" (Mark 10:5). So the certificate was never the dream. It was a rule written for hard hearts. Then Jesus takes us back to the beginning, where "the two will become one flesh," and says, "Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate" (Mark 10:8, 10:9). Marriage is something God joins, so it's never a deal we get to wiggle out of when the oven gets hot.

Now, I think this one hits close to home for a lot of people, and I want to say that gently. If this passage stings, I don't think it's here to pile on you. I think it shows how seriously God takes marriage and how seriously He takes the people in it, including the one who gets sent away (Mark 10:11-12). So hold marriage the way God holds it, with an open hand and a soft heart. Hard hearts were the problem back then, baker, and a soft one is still the fix.
